title: Finite exponential degree bound
statement:
Let $m,k$ be nonnegative integers with $m\ge1$, and let $A,M\in\mathbb R$ be nonnegative and $B\in\mathbb R$ be positive. Set $t=(2m+1)/(m+1)$. If $(t-1)^kB\le M^{2/t}$ and $M\le A^{2-t}B^{t-1}$, then
\[
B\le\left((1+1/m)^{m+1}\right)^{2k}A^2.
\]
replaced: Let $m\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ be integers, let $A,M\ge0$ and $B>0$, and put $t=(2m+1)/(m+1)$. If $(t-1)^kB\le M^{2/t}$ and $M\le A^{2-t}B^{t-1}$, then $B\le((1+1/m)^{m+1})^{2k}A^2$.
